newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-SLOW AND STEADY WINS RACE AS WAKEFIELD OUTDUELS JOHNSON.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-SLOW AND STEADY WINS RACE AS WAKEFIELD OUTDUELS JOHNSON.

text.p: Slow and, on this night, steady won the race Tuesday as knuckleballer Tim Wakefield outdueled fireballing Randy Johnson and the Boston Red Sox blanked the heavy-hitting Seattle Mariners 4-0.
The tantalizingly slow-throwing Wakefield, backed by a two-run homer by Mo Vaughn, tossed his second shutout of the month as the Red Sox defeated Johnson for the first time in over five years.
Johnson (14-3) was 7-0 with a 1.78 ERA in nine starts against Boston since his last loss to the Red Sox on May 1992.

"I just tried to throw as many strikes as I could," said Wakefield, who some outings has no control over his fluttering money pitch. "Going against him (Johnson), I knew I had to match him inning for inning and zero for zero."

Jesus Tavarez and Nomar Garciaparra led off the fifth with consecutive doubles off Johnson to snap a scoreless tie. One out later, Vaughn drove a 2-2 pitch over the centre-field wall for his 24th homer.
It was only the second homer by a left-handed batter this season off the left-handed Johnson, who allowed four runs on seven hits with nine strikeouts in seven innings.

"The thing about Johnson and his fastball is that you got to be willing to take one to get one," said Vaughn, who was hit by a pitch in the first inning. "He's very tough, you never feel comfortable against him. He throws hard and he has the ability to come inside.
"You've got to be willing to stay in there."
Red Sox manager Jimy Williams praised his pitcher. "That's a tough outfit we're playing against, they lead the majors in runs scored. To shut them down like that is something."
Johnson saluted Wakefield as well.
"I'm not ashamed today, the sun will rise tomorrow," Johnson said. "I didn't pitch a good game, that's all. Wakefield pitched a much better game, he deserved to win."

In Cleveland, Chuck Finley became the all-time team leader in wins with a three-hitter and Jack Howell hit two home runs for the second time in three games as the red-hot Anaheim Angels recorded a 7-2 victory over the Cleveland Indians.
Finley (10-6), in winning his seventh consecutive start, broke a tie with Nolan Ryan with his 139th win as an Angel.
"I really haven't thought about it," admitted Finley when asked about surpassing Ryan. "Just to be mentioned with Nolan Ryan is something right there."
Anaheim, who have won the first three games of the series and 17 of their last 22 games, moved within 1-1/2 games of Seattle in the West.

In Baltimore, Rafael Palmeiro capped a four-run fourth inning with a two-run double and Cal Ripken added a solo homer in the seventh, leading the Baltimore Orioles to their fourth straight win, 5-4 over the Texas Rangers.
The Orioles took the lead for good with four runs in the fourth off starter Jose Alberro (0-2), helped by some shoddy defence by Texas.

Rick Krivda (1-0), recalled from the minors Monday, allowed three runs and five hits over 5 1/3 innings to win his first appearance of the season. Randy Myers, the sixth Orioles pitcher used, notched his 29th save in 30 chances.
In New York, Paul O'Neill hit a three-run homer in the first inning and Dwight Gooden survived five rocky innings as the New York Yankees defeated the Oakland Athletics 7-4.
O'Neill's 15th homer off Oakland starter Carlos Reyes staked New York to a 3-0 lead. He added a sacrifice fly in a three-run second and has 21 hits in his last 52 at-bats.
Gooden (4-3) got the win despite surrendering four runs and seven hits in five innings.

In Kansas City, Marty Cordova hit a pair of two-run homers and the Minnesota Twins scored eight times in the third inning on the way to an 11-8 victory over the Kansas City Royals that snapped a four-game losing streak.

With the Royals ahead 3-0 after two innings, the Twins erupted for their biggest inning of the season. Cordova belted a homer, Rich Becker had a two-run triple, Ron Coomer a two-run single and Paul Molitor added an RBI single in the outburst against Ricky Bones (1-3).
LaTroy Hawkins (3-6) benefited from the scoring spree.

In Milwaukee, Mike Matheny had a two-run single in the fourth inning and Scott Karl allowed two runs in seven innings as the Brewers beat Toronto 4-2 to complete a doubleheader sweep of the Blue Jays for the second time in as many days.
Rookie Todd Dunn had a career-high three hits -- including a solo homer -- for Milwaukee, winners of seven straight.
Karl (6-10), who won his fourth consecutive start.
In the opener, Jose Mercedes threw seven shutout innings for his first win in over a month and Gerald Williams homered to lift the Brewers to a 2-0 win.
Mercedes (4-6), who had lost his last four decisions, allowed just three hits and did not walk a batter.

In Chicago, Willie Blair pitched a three-hitter for his first complete game in almost four years and Damion Easley homered and drove in three runs as the Detroit Tigers handed the slumping Chicago White Sox their fourth straight loss, 3-1.
Blair improved to 10-4, while James Baldwin fell to 7-11 for Chicago, who have lost six of their last seven games.
